text.S1: Once there was a miller who was poor, but who had a beautiful daughter. Now it happened that he had to go and speak to the King, and in order to make himself appear important he said to him, "I have a daughter who can spin straw into gold." The King said to the miller, "That is an art which pleases me well; if your daughter is as clever as you say, bring her tomorrow to my palace and I will try what she can do."
text.S2: Once there was a miller who was poor, but who had a beautiful daughter. Now it happened that he had to go and speak with the King, and in order to make himself appear important he said to him, "I have a daughter who can spin straw into gold." The King said to the miller, "That is a gift which pleases me a lot; if your daughter is as clever as you say, bring her tomorrow to my palace and I will try what she can do."
text.T1: Kale kale, panali munthu wogaya ufa amene anali wosauka, koma yemwe anali ndi mwana wamkaziwokongola. Tsopano, zinangotero kuti iwo amafunika kupita ndi kukalankhulana ndi Mfumu yaikulu, ndipo pofuna kuti awoneke ofunikira iwo anati kwa mfumuyo,“Ndili ndi mwana amene amapota udzu kukhala mwala wa golide.’’ Mfumu yaikuluyoinati kwawogaya ufa, “Iyo ndi mphatso imene indikondweretsa kwambiri; ndipo ngati mwana wanu wamkazi ndiwocenjera monga mmenemukuneneramu, mukabwere naye mawa kunyumba yanga, ndipo ndidzayesa cimene angacite”

text.S1: And when the girl was brought to him he took her into a room which was quite full of straw, gave her a spinning-wheel and a reel, and said, "Now set to work, and if by tomorrow morning early you have not spun this straw into gold during the night, you must die." Thereupon he himself locked up the room, and left her in it alone. So there sat the poor miller's daughter, and for the life of her could not tell what to do; she had no idea how straw could be spun into gold, and she grew more and more miserable, until at last she began to weep.
text.S2: And when the girl was brought to him he took her into a room which had a lot of straw, she was given a spinning-wheel and a reel, and said, "Now start working, and if by tomorrow morning early you have not spun this straw into gold during the night, you must die." Thereupon he himself locked up the room, and left her in it alone. So there sat the poor miller's daughter, and for the life of her could not tell what to do; she had no idea how straw could be spun into gold, and she was really worried until in end she began to weep.
text.T1: Ndiye pamene mtsikana anabwera kwa Mfumuyo, anamupereka m’cipinda momwe munali udzu wambiri, anamupatsa gudumu lopotera ndi cokulungira, ndipo anati, “Tsopano yambako kugwira nchito, ndipo ngati podzafika mawa m’mawa sudzapotaudzu uwu usiku kukhala golide uyenera kufa” Nthawi yomweyo Mfumu inatseka citseko cacipinda, ndi kumusiya yekha. Conco, anakhala pansi mwana wa wogaya ufa, ndipo pamoyo wake sanadziwe cocita; ndipo analibe ganizo lililonse lammene angapotere udzu kukhala golide, ndipo anada nkhawa kwambiri, pothera pake anayamba kulira.

text.S1: But all at once the door opened, and in came a little man, and said, "Good evening, Mistress Miller; why are you crying so?" "Alas!" answered the girl, "I have to spin straw into gold, and I do not know how to do it." "What will you give me," said the manikin, "if I do it for you?" "My necklace," said the girl. The little man took the necklace, seated himself in front of the wheel, and "whirr, whirr, whirr," three turns, and the reel was full; then he put another on, and whirr, whirr, whirr, three times round, and the second was full too. And so it went on until the morning, when all the straw was spun, and all the reels were full of gold.

text.S1: By daybreak the King was already there, and when he saw the gold he was astonished and delighted, but his heart became only moregreedy. He had the miller's daughter taken into another room full of straw, which was much larger, and commanded her to spin that also in one night if she valued her life. The girl knew not how to help herself, and was crying, when the door again opened, and the little man appeared, and said, "What will you give me if I spin that straw into gold for you?" "The ring on my finger," answered the girl.

text.T1: Podzafika m’mawa Mfumu yaikuluinali itabwera kale, ndipo itawona golide inadabwa kwambiri ndipo inakondwera, koma mtima wake unacita umbombo kwambiri. Mfumu yaikulu inapereka mwana wamkazi wawopanga ufa m’cipinda cina momwe munali udzu wambiri, udzu waukulu, ndikumulamula kuti apote golide wina ngati amakondadi moyo wake. Mtsikana analibe njira iliyonse momwe akanadzithandizira, ndipo amangolira, pamene citseko cinatsekukanso ndipokamwamuna kamatsengakanaonekanso, ndipo kanati, “Kodi mudzandipatsa ciyani ngati napanga golide kucokera ku udzu?’’ “Ndidzakupatsani mphete ili pacala canga,” anayankha mtsikanayo.

text.S1: The King rejoiced beyond measure at the sight, but still he had not gold enough; and he had the miller's daughter taken into a still larger room full of straw, and said, "You must spin this, too, in the course of this night; but if you succeed, you shall be my wife." "Even if she be a miller's daughter," thought he, "I could not find a richer wife in the whole world."

text.S1: When the girl was alone the manikin came again for the third time, and said, "What will you give me if I spin the straw for you this time also?" "I have nothing left that I could give," answered the girl. "Then promise me, if you should become Queen, your first child." "Who knows whether that will ever happen?" thought the miller's daughter; and, not knowing how else to help herself in this strait, she promised the manikin what he wanted, and for that he once more span the straw into gold.

text.S1: And when the King came in the morning, and found all as he had wished, he took her in marriage, and the pretty miller's daughter became a Queen.

text.S1: A year after, she had a beautiful child, and she never gave a thought to the manikin. But suddenly he came into her room, and said, "Now give me what you promised." The Queen was horror-struck, and offered the manikin all the riches of the kingdom if he would leave her the child. But the manikin said, "No, something that is living is dearer to me than all the treasures in the world." Then the Queen began to weep and cry, so that the manikin pitied her. "I will give you three days' time," said he, "if by that time you find out my name, then shall you keep your child."

text.T1: Patapita caka cimodzi, iye anakhala ndi mwana wokongola, ndipo sanaganizireko za kamwamuna kamatsenga kaja. Koma mwadzidzizi kanalowa m’cipinda cake, ndipo kanati; “Tsopano ndipatse zomwe unandilonjeza” Mfumukazi anagwidwa ndi mantha, ndipo anakauuza kamwamuna kamatsenga kaja kuti akapatse cuma conse ca m’dziko ngati angamusiye ndi mwana. Kamwamuna kamatsenga kajakanati, “Ayi, cinthu ca moyo ndi cabwino kuposa cuma cam’dziko lonse lapansi.” Mfumukazi inayamba kusisima ndi kulira, kotero kuti kanamumvera cifundo.” Ndidzakupatsa nthawi masiku atatu” kanatero, “ ngati panthawiyo udzadziwa dzina langa, ndiye kuti udzasunga mwana wakoyo.”

text.S1: So the Queen thought the whole night of all the names that she had ever heard, and she sent a messenger over the country to inquire, far and wide, for any other names that there might be. When the manikin came the next day, she began with Caspar, Melchior, Balthazar, and said all the names she knew, one after another; but to every one the little man said, "That is not my name." On the second day she had inquiries made in the neighborhood as to the names of the people there, and she repeated to the manikin the most uncommon and curious. "Perhaps your name is Shortribs, or Sheepshanks, or Laceleg?" but he always answered, "That is not my name."

text.T1: Mfumukazi inaganizira usiku wonse maina amene inamvako, ndipo inatuma kazembe kuti akafunse m’dziko lonse, kutali ndi pafupi, pamaina onse amene angapezeke. Pamene kamwamuna kamatsenga kaja kanabwera tsiku lotsatira, Mfumukazi inayamba kuchula maina awa, Caspar, Melchoir, Balthazar ndipo inachula maina onse amene imadziwa, dzina pa dzina; koma kamwamuna kamatsenga kajakanakana, nati, “Limenelo sidzina langa.” Patsiku lachiwiri Mfumukazi anali atafunsa kwa anthu amene amakhala nawo pamaina omwe anali nawo anthukumene kuja, anabwereza kwakamwamuna kamatsenga kaja pochula maina omwe ali osafala ndiocititsa cidwi. “Kapena dzina lanu ndi Shortribs, kapena Sheepshanks, kapena Laceleg?’’ koma iko kankayankha kuti, “Ilo sidzina langa.”

text.S1: On the third day the messenger came back again, and said, "I have not been able to find a single new name, but as I came to a high mountain at the end of the forest, where the fox and the hare bid each other good night, there I saw a little house, and before the house a fire was burning, and round about the fire quite a ridiculous little man was jumping: he hopped upon one leg, and shouted—"To-day I bake, to-morrow brew, The next I'll have the young Queen's child. Ha! glad am I that no one knew That Rumpelstiltskin I am styled."

text.S2: You may think how glad the Queen was when she heard the name! And when soon afterwards the little man came in, and asked, "Now, Mistress Queen, what is my name?" at first she said, "Is your name Conrad?" "No." "Is your name Harry?" "No." "Perhaps your name is Rumpelstiltskin?"

text.T2: Mungaganize mmeneMfumukazi anakondwera atamva za dzina lake!Posacedwa kamwamuna kamatsenga kajakanabwera, ndipo kanafunsa kuti, “Tsopano, Amayi Mfumukazi, dzina langa ndi ndani?” poyamba iye anati, “Kodi ndinua Conrad?” “Ayi.” Kodi dzina lako ndiwe Harry?” “Ayi” “Kapena dzina lako ndiwe Rumpelstiltskin?’’

text.S1: "The devil has told you that! the devil has told you that!" cried the little man, and in his anger he plunged his right foot so deep into the earth that his whole leg went in; and then in rage he pulled at his left leg so hard with both hands that he tore himself in two.

text.T1: “Satana wakuuza eti! Satana zoona wakuuza eti!” kanalira kamwamuna kamatsenga kaja, ndipo ndi ukali wake kanadzambwira phazi lake munthaka kotero kuti mwendo wake wonse unambira; ndipo guza mwendowake wamanzere ndi manja ake awiri kucokera mwamphamvu m’nthakairi ndipo anadzidula pawiri.
text.T2: “Satana wakuuza eti! Satana zoona wakuuza eti!” kanalira kamwamuna kamatsenga kaja, ndipo ndi ukali wake kanaguza mwendo wake wamanzere ndi manja ake awiri kucokera mwamphamvu m’nthakairi ndipo anadzidula pawiri.
